+### Read-only service pilot contract gate
+
+1. Compare current official documentation with the selected release's public-route implementation before writing the adapter. Record documented fields, pinned-source fields and observed live fields separately; a resolved image digest does not establish a running version or signed source-to-image provenance.
+2. Establish the upstream credential's actual read scope before any real request. Require explicit approval for organization-wide reads even when the adapter returns only one account; local filtering cannot narrow what the upstream credential reads. Review endpoint semantics, not merely GET verbs, and exclude account-connection and authorization-initiation routes.
+3. Build a field mapping with source, conversion, missing-value behavior and access predicate. Do not fabricate attempts, content versions, artifact links or actual publication times to satisfy an existing fixture schema. Preserve missing relationships and raw unknown statuses; scheduled time and query failure are not evidence of publication time or a publishing attempt.
+4. Inspect recurrence expansion and pagination in the pinned public handler. Repeated record IDs need an explicit omission/partial policy or rejection, not invented occurrence IDs; absence of a cursor is not proof that a returned projection is complete.
+5. Keep fixture authorization distinct from a bounded real pilot contract. Do not promote test-only permission keys or source-declared grants into server authority. Validate the owner-local identity and stable Project/account mapping independently, and disclose the single-user boundary rather than claiming multi-tenant authorization.
+6. Report static contract review, synthetic adapter tests, empty-instance readiness, real account reads, real record reads and real artifact-link verification as separate evidence classes. An incomplete adapter is blocked implementation, not merely missing real credentials. Finish authorized offline evidence delivery while leaving denied operations stopped; do not turn setup errors into behavioral test results.
